exposure: Adjusted for age, parity, and previous cesarean delivery
Planned ECV vs. no planned ECV
cohort: 298 patients with breech presentations between 33 and 35 weeks of amenorrhea followed at a university hospital and delivered after 35 weeks, between January 1st, 2011 and December 31st, 2013
finding: Planned external cephalic version (ECV) in a center with a high rate of successful vaginal breech delivery (61.1%) did not significantly impact the cesarean section rate.
